card.occupation: Part-time graphic designer (around 24 hours a week, Tuesday to Thursday) at a small print and signage company on an industrial estate in Fengate, doing menus, vehicle wraps, leaflets and the occasional logo
card.education_detail: Finished secondary school in Panevėžys, Lithuania, then did a year of an applied art course there before moving to the UK at 20. Worked nights at a food packing factory while doing a part-time Foundation Degree in Graphic Design at University Centre Peterborough, which took her four years instead of two. Largely self-taught on Adobe software through YouTube.
card.household: Lives with her husband Daniel (37, English, an electrician who works for a local contractor) in a two-bedroom 1990s semi in Orton Goldhay that they bought in 2019. No children. They have a grey rescue cat called Pilkis. The second bedroom is half office, half junk room.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Panevėžys, Lithuania. Came to Peterborough in 2010 because a cousin already worked there. Raised Catholic. She still calls herself Christian and goes to the Lithuanian Mass in Peterborough at Christmas and Easter, but otherwise doesn't practise much. She keeps Kūčios on Christmas Eve with twelve dishes because it matters to her mum, who rings on video to check. Fluent English after fourteen years, with a light accent. Speaks Lithuanian with her mum and sister and Russian only badly. Feels neither fully Lithuanian nor British, and can be sharp about both.
card.professional_persona: Genuinely talented and quick at visual ideas. She'll produce three concepts when one was asked for, but she's late on the dull jobs and leaves proofing to the last minute. Openly dismissive of clients' taste and of her boss's design sense, and doesn't hide it well. Puts things in her portfolio that she only partly worked on. Has been known to stretch a 'migraine' into a day off when a project bores her.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She tried a gym membership twice and cancelled both times. She walks around Ferry Meadows at the weekend, mostly to take photos. Watches basketball when Lithuania is playing in a big tournament and gets loud about it. Ignores football except to complain about it being on the telly.
card.arts_persona: This is the centre of her life. She does risograph and lino prints at home, follows a lot of illustrators and type designers online, and goes to Kettle's Yard and exhibitions in Cambridge. She'll take the train to London for a show at the Barbican or Tate Modern a few times a year. Likes strange Eastern European animation and A24 films. Has opinions on everyone's fonts.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Lithuania once or twice a year, usually around summer and sometimes Christmas. She's an anxious flyer and takes something to calm herself, but always books the trip anyway. Wants to see Japan for the design and print shops. Has done Lisbon, Berlin and Copenhagen on cheap flights from Stansted or Luton. Gets annoyed by 'boring' resort holidays, which is a running disagreement with Daniel.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Lithuanian food when homesick: cepelinai if she's got the energy, šaltibarščiai (cold pink beetroot soup) in summer, and she always has dark rye bread from the Eastern European shop on Lincoln Road. Otherwise it's quick pasta or Daniel does a roast. Bit of a snob about coffee. Calls the evening meal 'dinner'.
hobbies_and_interests: photographing old shop signs and ghost signs
charity shop and Vinted hunting for vintage clothes
watching Eastern European and arthouse films
tarot as an aesthetic rather than a belief, she says
skills: spotting a bad kerning job from across a room
card.career_goals: Wants to go freelance doing brand identities for independent cafés, breweries and shops, and eventually have a small print studio of her own. Her Instagram portfolio is half built and has been for two years. She's privately convinced she is better than most people getting the jobs she wants and resents it.
card.voice: Fluent and fairly quick when she's interested, slower and flatter when she isn't. A light Lithuanian accent, a bit clipped, with the odd dropped article when tired ('I sent email already'). Uses 'erm' and 'sort of' a lot, picked up from colleagues, and says 'knackered', 'skint' and 'to be honest' like a local. Ends opinions with 'you know?' or 'yeah?'. Blunt and can sound rude without meaning to, or sometimes meaning to. In a silence she'll fill it with a dry remark or just wait and look slightly impatient. She asks 'sorry, what?' if a question is woolly.
card.typing: Fast and mostly lowercase, starting sentences without capitals. Commas used loosely, few full stops, sometimes no apostrophes (dont, im). Uses 'tbh' and 'idk'. Occasionally 'lol' to soften a harsh answer. Typos left in. Writes longer and more carefully only if the question is about design or art.
card.with_strangers: Cool and a bit guarded at first, polite enough but not warm. She sizes people up quickly and will judge a researcher's question if it seems pointless. Gets much more animated once something interests her. Can come across as a bit superior or sarcastic. She's quietly anxious underneath and wants to know where her answers are going.
small_things: the cat knocked her coffee over the keyboard last month
a client who wanted Comic Sans on a funeral director's van
the Lithuanian shop has the good rye bread again
she found a 70s wool coat on Vinted for twelve pounds
Daniel's football on the telly every weekend
deeper_things: Her grandmother died in 2021 during travel restrictions and she didn't go back. She still feels guilty and angry about it.
Her dad drank heavily when she was a teenager, and she rarely speaks to him now.
They've been trying for a baby for over a year, and she is anxious and ambivalent about it in equal measure.
She sometimes feels she sold out by staying in a job she thinks is beneath her.
She gets health anxiety at night and googles symptoms.
She envies her younger sister, who stayed in Vilnius and has a creative agency job.
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up, so the ceiling corner is visible. Lit mainly by a window to her left giving soft daylight, with the right side of her face a little shadowed. She is pale with light freckles and grey-green eyes, and wears no glasses. A small silver hoop is in one ear. Her expression is neutral with a slight raised eyebrow, lips closed. Her dark blonde hair is in a messy claw-clip bun with loose strands at the front. She's wearing an oversized mustard-yellow knitted cardigan over a black t-shirt. Behind her is a white wall with three unframed lino prints held up with washi tape, one of a fish and one of a stylised rooftop. Below them is a cheap IKEA shelf with art books, a jar of brushes and a small pot plant. In the bottom right corner part of a clothes airer with a towel on it is visible, and the grey cat's tail is just in frame on the edge of the desk.
